business_problem: As Italy's national agency for workplace health and safety, INAIL holds sensitive personal information and needed stronger defenses against growing phishing campaigns, sophisticated malware, and potential data breaches, along with more current threat intelligence and automated analysis.
solution_summary: INAIL worked with DXC to implement an automated cyber-threat intelligence and analysis platform centered on IOC ingestion, search, and machine-learning scoring. Upstream, open-source intelligence sources and multiple security intelligence engines feed threat data, email/domain/user lookups, and suspicious attachment evidence into leading security software and a search engine. MineMeld aggregates indicators of compromise from multiple sources and converts them into consistent configuration lists that INAIL's security workflow can redistribute to downstream security tools. For analysis, classifier systems and a machine learning model extract characteristics from domains and URLs to perform predictive reputation analysis and phishing detection at scale, including automated analysis on millions of URLs and domains. The solution is served through an external integration layer for technical users and a self-service malware analysis solution for 11,000 nontechnical users; the source does not name a separate storage product, so normalized threat data appears to be managed within the workflow while exchanges with other national security bodies are automated.

data_flow: Open-source intelligence sources and security intelligence engines supply IOC and reputation data to leading security software, the search engine, and MineMeld. The platform normalizes indicators, runs classifier systems and a machine learning model on domains and URLs, then redistributes vetted IOC lists to INAIL's security tools. Technical users access outputs through the external integration layer, while employees use the malware analysis interface for self-service attachment checks.
